newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-PRASAD JOLTS S.AFRICA WITH TEST BEST 6-10.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PRASAD JOLTS S.AFRICA WITH TEST BEST 6-10.

text.p: Indian medium-pacer Venkatesh Prasad produced his best bowling performance in test cricket of six for 104 to lead a fightback against South Africa on Thursday.
Prasad's sustained effort sent South Africa crashing from their overnight 339 for two to 428 all out on the second day of the second test.
India had lost opener Rahul Dravid by tea when the home country, who lead 1-0 in the three-test series, were 70 for one.
Dravid, having hit six fours in his 31, needlessly tried to cut a wide and high delivery from Brian McMillan, and Andrew Hudson at second slip held a good head-high catch.

India's first-wicket pair had scored freely, equalling their country's previous best opening stand against South Africa of 68 between Ravi Shastri and Ajay Jadeja at Johannesburg in the 1992-93 series.

South Africa's hopes of a mammoth first innings total were dashed in the morning as Prasad added five wickets to the one he took on the opening day, and leg-spinner Anil Kumble helped to polish off the tail with two wickets.
Prasad, playing in his sixth test, improved his best test figures of five for 76 against England at Lord's last June.
Javagal Srinath, the hero of India's victory in the first test at Ahmedabad, had two for 107 and Kumble two for 78.
